name: Accountable, or not?
note: You can delegate the typing, not the accountability. Pick the response that owns AI-assisted work rather than hiding behind the tool.

items.prompt: A bug ships in AI-generated code. In the postmortem, what's the accountable response?
candidates: 'I approved it. I reviewed it against X and Y but missed the empty-input case; here's the gate I'm adding so it can't recur.' — owns the approval, shows what was checked, names the gap, fixes the process
'The AI generated that part.' — true, and not a defense; accountability doesn't transfer to the tool
'The tests passed, so it's not my fault.' — green tests you didn't design don't transfer ownership
'I'll be more careful next time.' — no provenance, no process fix
items.correct: 'I approved it. I reviewed it against X and Y but missed the empty-input case; here's the gate I'm adding so it can't recur.' — owns the approval, shows what was checked, names the gap, fixes the process
items.explanation: Approval is ownership. The accountable response owns it, shows the provenance (what was checked), names the gap honestly, and fixes the process. 'The AI wrote it' is the non-defense.
items.principle: 'The AI wrote it' is not an answer — approval is ownership.

items.prompt: What is 'provenance' for code you generated with AI and shipped yourself?
candidates: Your ability to explain and defend it — what you reviewed it against and verified — is your provenance; comprehension and verification (the loop) are what let you stand behind AI-written code as your own
A comment saying '// generated by AI' at the top of the file
The saved chat log of your prompts to the AI
Nothing — provenance only matters for teams
items.correct: Your ability to explain and defend it — what you reviewed it against and verified — is your provenance; comprehension and verification (the loop) are what let you stand behind AI-written code as your own
items.explanation: For individual work, provenance is your demonstrable understanding plus your verification record — not a label or a chat log. The loop is what produces it.
items.principle: Your provenance is that you can explain and defend it — the loop is how you earn that.

items.prompt: In a regulated system (fintech/health), what does accountability for AI-written code require beyond 'it works'?
candidates: An explicit record — what was AI-generated, what it was tested against, who reviewed and approved it — provenance as documentation, because 'the model decided' is not an acceptable audit answer
Nothing extra; if it passes the tests it's compliant
A disclaimer noting that AI was used in development
The vendor of the AI tool is accountable, not you
items.correct: An explicit record — what was AI-generated, what it was tested against, who reviewed and approved it — provenance as documentation, because 'the model decided' is not an acceptable audit answer
items.explanation: Regulated contexts require documented provenance: the generation, the testing, and the approval chain. Passing tests alone, disclaimers, and vendor-blame don't satisfy accountability.
items.principle: In regulated systems, accountability requires documented provenance, not just a green build.
